::: {#lem-trail-ends}
#### Ends of the edges of a trail

Let $v_0, e_1, v_1, \ldots, e_n, v_n$ be a trail (@def-trail) in a graph (@def-graph-vertices-edges), and let $w$ be a vertex.
Count the ends at $w$ of the edges $e_1, \ldots, e_n$, as in the proof of @thm-handshake.

- If the trail starts and ends at the same vertex, $v_0 = v_n$, then the count is even.
- If $v_0 \ne v_n$, then the count is odd for $w = v_0$ and for $w = v_n$, and even for every other $w$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

The edge $e_i$ has one end at $v_{i - 1}$ and its other end at $v_i$,
both at the same vertex when $e_i$ is a loop.
The edges $e_1, \ldots, e_n$ are all different, so no end is counted twice.
Let $k$ be the number of indices $i$ with $1 \le i \le n - 1$ and $v_i = w$,
and write $[P]$ for 1 if $P$ is true and 0 if $P$ is false.
The ends at $v_{i - 1}$, for $i = 1, \ldots, n$, give $k + [v_0 = w]$ ends at $w$,
and the ends at $v_i$, for $i = 1, \ldots, n$, give $k + [v_n = w]$ ends at $w$.
So the count is

$$
2k + [v_0 = w] + [v_n = w].
$$

If $v_0 = v_n$, the last two terms are equal, so the count is even.
If $v_0 \ne v_n$, the last two terms add up to 1 when $w$ is $v_0$ or $v_n$, and to 0 otherwise.

:::

:::
